headline: Sales growth outpaced by cost inflation, squeezing margins
summary_short: Performance Food Group's fiscal Q3 2026 (three months ended March 28, 2026) net sales rose 6.4% y/y to $16.29 billion on higher case volumes and inflation-driven pricing, but net income fell 28.5% y/y to $41.7 million ($0.27 diluted EPS) as operating expenses grew 8.6% y/y, faster than gross profit.
summary_long: Net sales growth was driven by a 4.4% rise in case volume (organic +3.7%), favorable case mix, and ~4.5% product cost inflation passed through in pricing. Gross profit rose in step (+6.4% y/y) on procurement efficiencies and channel mix. Operating expenses climbed 8.6% y/y on personnel costs (+$71.7M), acquisition/debt-related fees (+$10.1M), depreciation (+$15.8M), and fuel expense (+$7.8M), compressing operating income 14.6% and net income 28.5% y/y, partly offset by a $9.6M unrealized fuel-collar gain. The company repaid $1.1B of Notes due 2027 and issued $1.1B of new Notes due 2034, leaving long-term debt down 5.6% y/y. Cash was $56.1M versus $86.7M at fiscal year-end. No forward guidance was stated.

drivers.explanation: Company-disclosed: growth primarily driven by an increase in cases sold, including a favorable shift in mix of cases sold, and an increase in selling price per case as a result of inflation.
Company-disclosed: increase primarily driven by cost of goods sold optimization through procurement efficiencies and a favorable mix shift toward the higher-margin independent channel.
Derived-arithmetic: operating expenses rose 8.6% y/y (personnel, professional fees, D&A, fuel) faster than the 6.4% gross profit gain, compressing operating income despite higher sales.
Derived-arithmetic: EBITDA held roughly flat y/y (+0.4%) because higher depreciation and amortization added back offset most of the y/y decline in operating income.
Company-disclosed: decline primarily driven by an increase in operating expenses, partially offset by increases in gross profit and other income due to unrealized gains on fuel collars.
Derived-arithmetic: diluted EPS fell 27.0% y/y, a smaller drop than the 28.5% net income decline because weighted diluted shares rose only 0.3% y/y.
Not explained separately in the release; decline follows the operating-expense growth cited for net income, plus higher interest expense from increased average borrowings including finance leases.
Company-disclosed: the company repaid $1.1 billion of 5.500% Senior Notes due 2027 and issued $1.1 billion of new Notes due 2034, a refinancing that left funded debt modestly lower y/y.

Company-disclosed: fiscal Q3 2026 net sales grew 6.4% y/y but operating expense growth of 8.6% (personnel, acquisitions, D&A, fuel) outpaced it, compressing operating income 14.6% and net income 28.5% y/y despite an unrealized fuel-collar gain.
